title: fix(metadata)!: the boot priming pass primes every holder of a name two packages hold, of a type stored per (package, name), so a bare read of that name is refused after the pass as without it

_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg?thread=cmsg_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wgPrTjDBPZcfALKmAFE29GLi)_

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：接了数据库加载器的宿主，启动预载对 `api`、`agent`、`skill`、`action`、`permission` 这五类，只要一个名字有两个以上的包持有，就把每个包的那一项都载进注册表；只有一个包持有的名字照旧只载一项。两包同名旁边的无包行不盖宿主包戳，留在裸槽（契约复核 F1）。
- 为什么改：两个包同名时，启动后不带包名的读取答了最后存的那个包的正文，没有报歧义（史诗 #31527 红线 2）；只按列绑定的行，列表里还少了另一个包。
- 风险与回滚：收窄（BREAKING）：启动后裸读两包同名项、以及没有合并清单时 runtime 的裸 `/actions` 调用，原来拿到其中一个包的，现在 409 并点名两个包；无包行最后保存时，点名一个不持有该名字的包的读取，原来答无包行，现在答空。都和不预载时一样。单持有者（包括无包定制行、宿主声明包名的情况）每个答案都不动，有实测 CONTROL 钉。仓库里没有组合接数据库加载器，第一方调用方 0，库里的行不增不改。回滚即 revert。
- 先看：`packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts` 的 `namesSeveralPackagesHold` 与 `pluralEntryKey`（只在两包以上同名时按包分项），`database-loader.ts` 的 `unscopedTypeRows`，`metadata-manager.ts` 的 `loadMany` / `loadManyKeyed` 与 `withLoaderEntryPackages`（两包同名时按内容配对盖包戳），`plugin.ts` 的 `primingOrder`。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata exec vitest run src/loaders/database-loader.test.ts -t '#32521'`，应见 49 passed。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

Fixes #32521

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — on a host that wires a `DatabaseLoader` (none in the workspace), after the boot priming pass a read naming no package (`MetadataManager.get`, `getDiagnosed`) of an `api`, `agent`, `skill`, `action` or `permission` whose name two packages' stored rows hold is refused `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` (`ambiguous-in-environment`, naming both), where it served the body of the row saved last; the same read without the pass already refused. Beside a package-less row of that name saved last, a read naming a package that holds none of its rows answers nothing, as without the pass, where it served that row (row 7a). The runtime's bare `/actions` door with no merged listing is refused the same way (row 8). Every other moved answer hands on or registers more holders and refuses nothing. No answer for a name one package holds moves.
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: updated — `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx` (`loadManyKeyed`): its stamp paragraph (#32548) said a body is stamped only when no other body carries its name; a name two or more packages hold is now handed on once per holder, each body stamped with its own row's package. No skill teaches how many holders `loadMany` hands on or what a bare read answers after a boot over a `DatabaseLoader`.

`Metadata-protocol: none` because no key, value, requirement or type a metadata author writes moves; only what the manager hands on and registers at boot does (the #29029 and #32458 precedent).

**Narrowing: yes**, three faces (rows 1, 7a and 8). First-party callers: **0**. `MetadataManager` wires a `DatabaseLoader` only through `config.driver` (with `config.datasource`), `setDatabaseDriver` or `setDataEngine`, and no package, app or example calls them (`git grep` at this head; `MetadataPlugin` builds its manager with neither).

## What changes

The epic seat's ruling, verbatim: "when two holders exist, a bare read answers 409 again after the boot preload, the same as without the preload (red line 2). The loadMany/loadManyKeyed answer change gets its own FROM → TO and a pin, plus a contract review. Unfiltered list reads keep every holder." Its follow-up on the single-holder shapes: a package-less row under a name one package holds is that holder's customization (ADR-0150 D4, #32183 ruling A) and is served as usual, including on a host whose declared package is that holder; no single-holder answer moves (red line 3).

1. `namesSeveralPackagesHold` and `pluralEntryKey` (new, `package-slotted-store.ts`, not re-exported from the package entry): a plural read keeps one entry per store slot only for a name two or more packages hold among its entries; any other name keeps one entry per name, as before. An item held for no package is never counted as a holder. A bundled type keeps its `(package, name, member)` key.
2. `DatabaseLoader.unscopedTypeRows` (behind `loadMany` and `loadManyKeyed`): a name two or more packages' rows hold keeps one row per `(package, name)`, each slot's row saved last, FROM one row per name. Any other name: one row, the row saved last, as before.
3. `MetadataManager.loadMany`'s stamp (`withLoaderEntryPackages`, #32458): #32458 stamps a body only when one keyed entry and one body carry its name, so the two rows of a name two packages hold would be handed on unstamped and counted as no holder. A name a loader's keyed read holds for two or more packages now has each of its bodies stamped with the package of the keyed entry whose own body it is (the same content, each entry once) — only where that loader's bodies of the name are exactly its rows keyed by it (every such row's body carries the name, and as many bodies carry it as rows are keyed by it); otherwise none is stamped, so no body takes a package its row is not bound to (#32458's contract review F3).
4. `MetadataManager.loadMany` and `loadManyKeyed` read every loader first, then key by the same rule across all of them, an earlier loader's item kept over a later loader's of the same key. A loader with no `loadManyKeyed` is asked for every name it lists of a type stored per `(package, name)` (the later item may be another package's); for every other type it skips a name already answered, as before.
5. The boot priming pass (`MetadataPlugin._loadFromFileSystem`) registers, for an unbundled slotted type, the items a package holds first and then the package-less ones (`primingOrder`), so a package-less item beside two holders stays the name's bare slot (the environment's own item) and the registry holds what a read without the pass answers, whatever order the loaders hand them in. On a host that declares its package (`MetadataPluginOptions.packageId`), the pass does not stamp such an item with it (`contestedNames`): ADR-0150 D4 makes a package-less item a holder's customization only under a name one package holds, and stamped, the item was filed into the host's slot, over a holder's own item when the host is one of them (contract review F1), or as a third holder when it is not. A name one package holds keeps the stamp, so its customization is filed as before (C3).

`email_template` (bundled) already kept one row and one item per `(package, name, member)`; its path is untouched (CONTROL pin).

Why runtime is in scope: the Claim's file surface is `packages/metadata` plus the callers this needs. The runtime change is test-only. The door's code is untouched; its input, `MetadataManager.loadMany('action')`, moves (row 6), so the door's answer moves (row 8). The epic ruling requires every moved answer pinned with its arm, so that one is pinned at the door, over a real `MetadataManager` over a real `DatabaseLoader`, beside its single-holder CONTROLs.

## Why

On a host that wires a `DatabaseLoader`, the boot priming pass registered one item per name for these types, so after the boot a read naming no package of a name two packages hold answered the body of the row saved last instead of the `409` naming both that the same read answers without the pass (epic #31527 red line 2), and `list` dropped every holder but one. The epic seat's rulings bound the fix: every holder of such a name is kept and primed, and no answer for a name one package holds moves (red line 3).

## Moved answers (FROM → TO)

FROM is `origin/main` with #32458 landed (#32548, `0f9b5653`); the CONTROL expectations were measured at `efd4ea3a` (#32458's first head) and hold unchanged at main and at this head. TO is this head. First-party count 0 on every row: only a host that wires a `DatabaseLoader` (or another loader whose keyed read hands on two packages' items of a name) reaches any of them.

Not changed, and declared: a name no package or one package holds, on every reader above. `MemoryLoader loadMany/loadManyKeyed → covered by #32517` (it still answers one item per name for these types; `metadata-manager-match-endpoint.test.ts`, the door peer of the updated pin). `DatabaseLoader.load` and `list` still answer one per name.

## Acceptance notes

- Card pins: two holders → bare read `409` naming both, `list` holds both (row 1, row 3); one holder → served (C2, and C3–C5 for the customization shapes); CONTROL `email_template` unchanged (C1). Ablated (table above).
- Epic ruling (a): the single-holder package-less shape is served as before on every host (C3); nothing refuses it. The host-package refusal an earlier local draft carried is gone, so it has no row.
- Epic ruling (b): with no merged listing, a single holder's bare `/actions` call still answers that holder (C5); two holders are refused (row 8).
- Contract review F1 (6820408972): measured before the fix on a host declaring ALPHA, two holders and a package-less row: a read naming ALPHA answered the package-less body and `list` dropped ALPHA's item, in every order; on a host declaring another package the bare refusal named three packages. Fixed by the seat's preferred route (no host stamp on that item, so it stays in the bare slot); every read and `list` after the pass now equal the same reads without it over all 60 type × order × host shapes. F2 to F4 and the out-of-scope `action` row went to follow-up cards #32680 and #32681.

## Out-of-scope findings (reported, not changed)

- `MemoryLoader loadMany/loadManyKeyed → covered by #32517`: the artifact door's store still answers one item per name of these types from its own plural reads.
- An `action` row held for no package, bound to an object that only one of the name's two package holders binds: `DatabaseLoader` keys action rows per `(package, name)` whatever object (`storeRowWriteKey`), so it stores that row in the name's bare slot; the registry keys an action by object and name (`storeWriteKey`), so registering it after the packages files it as that holder's customization of that object. Measured (ALPHA `approve` on `account` v1, BETA on `contact` v2, a package-less one on `account` v3): after the pass a read naming ALPHA answers the package-less body, where the loaders' read without the pass answers ALPHA's own; a bare read is refused both ways. Before this change the pass registered the package-less row alone and the same read answered it too, so this answer does not move here. The split between the two keys predates this change (#32246); no first-party path writes such a row. Not changed here; the seat filed it as #32681.
